findings.title: Document replay semantics on the exported Node sink
findings.evidence: packages/node/src/v3-live.ts:381-394 exports V3AdmittedVertexSink without replay/idempotency guidance, while docs/production-hardening/production-hardening-tdd-plan-v2.md:100233-100237 requires the contract comment only beside CreateV3RoomSessionInput.onAcceptedVertex
findings.impact: Direct Node consumers can encounter the same recovered-delivery replay but will not see the room-level contract clarification, leaving the public low-level sink semantics ambiguous.
findings.required_action: f5b0v owner: mirror the replayable-attempt, digest-keyed idempotency, and fail-closed rejection guidance beside V3AdmittedVertexSink during the tests/comment-only GREEN, without changing its shape or behavior.

contract_assessment: The selected contract is technically honest: canonical projection deduplicates authenticated vertices by digest, while arbitrary external callback effects cannot be atomically coupled to the existing admission or issuance stores. Replayable authenticated notification with consumer-owned digest idempotency preserves fail-closed rejection, canonical ordering, recovery-before-issue, and owner cleanup. Durable external exactly-once would require the stated separately reviewed transactional application port.
consumer_assessment: The named production consumers do not contradict the contract: v3-chat and grid use no-op onAcceptedVertex callbacks, and the room migration collectors are session-local reconstruction observers checked against canonical projection/state. Live-journal and issuance-store types contain admission/issuance durability but no application-delivery acknowledgement transaction.
red_green_assessment: The signed two-row RED and validated self-excluding evidence are causal: only the two external-ledger assumptions fail, with d1,d1,d2 observed across failure and cold reopen while canonical state, operation accounting, authority, and cleanup remain intact. The proposed GREEN criteria retain hard canonical exact-once checks, explicitly assert replayable notification attempts, preserve failure controls, and require a complete consumer inventory and isolated evidence.
